transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I’m not overreacting or wasting your time, it's probably nothing too serious, but... I guess what brings me in is that I’ve just been feeling so tired lately. 

I mean, I'm a manager, so I'm used to being busy and I usually handle it fine, but recently I'm just exhausted in a way that sleep doesn't really seem to fix. It’s hard to explain, but even just getting through a normal workday and, you know, making it to dinner at home... it just feels a lot heavier than it should right now. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining about normal life, but... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be coming in for?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, even activities that you normally find pleasurable or interesting?

Well, um... maybe a little? I know everyone gets in a rut sometimes, so I try not to make a big deal out of it. But... I usually really love painting. And I normally enjoy wandering through museum exhibits, it's always been my favorite way to recharge. 

Lately, though, I just... I don't know, I leave my art supplies sitting there completely untouched. And I can’t seem to make myself care enough to actually go out to a gallery or anything. I feel a little guilty admitting that, honestly, like I'm just being lazy with my free time. Is that... is that a normal thing to happen when you're this exhausted? I hope I don't sound like I'm just giving up on my hobbies or anything.
Have you noticed feeling down or having a low mood most days, even when there’s nothing specific bothering you?

Um, well... I try really hard to keep a positive attitude, especially since my team relies on me to set a good tone at work. I don't want to sound ungrateful for what I have, because there's really nothing specific going wrong in my life right now. 

But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling a bit down. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but most days lately, I just wake up with this... this heavy, sort of gray feeling. It almost feels like I’m already disappointed in the day before it even starts. I try to just push through it and put on a brave face, but it's been tough to shake. I don't know, does that sound like just a normal bad mood to you? I really hope I'm not just being overly pessimistic.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your energy levels or an increase in fatigue, even after resting?

Um, yes, I think that's actually... that's kind of exactly what I meant earlier when I was saying why I came in. I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I know your time is valuable. 

But yes, the fatigue is... it's just so persistent. Like I mentioned, I’m just exhausted in this way that getting a full night's sleep doesn’t seem to fix at all. I try to just power through, you know, because as a manager I really need to be on top of things, but even just getting through a normal workday and then making it to dinner at home... it just feels so much heavier than it should right now. I don't want to sound weak or like I can't handle my responsibilities, but... is it normal to feel that drained even when you're trying your best to rest?
Can you tell me if you’ve completely lost interest in your hobbies, like painting or going to museums, or if you still care about them but just don’t feel like doing them right now?

Oh, um... I guess I sort of touched on that a little bit earlier, didn't I? Sorry, I hope I'm being helpful and actually answering your questions properly. 

It's... it's a little hard to explain without sounding like I'm just throwing in the towel. In my head, I know I still love those things. Like, I *want* to be the person who loves painting and wandering through the exhibits, because I usually do. But recently... I just look at my supplies sitting there untouched, and... I just can't make myself care enough to actually pick up a brush or go out to a museum. 

Is that... does that make sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just abandoning the things I love, or that I'm not trying. I'm sure it's just a temporary slump, right?
Have you found yourself being more self-critical lately, or feeling like you’re not good enough at things, even when others might see it differently?

Um, well... I really try not to be too hard on myself, because I know everyone makes mistakes. I want to be a good example for my team, and, you know, for my kids. I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself, because I know I have a lot to be thankful for. 

But... lately, yes, I suppose I have been a little more critical. It's embarrassing to admit, but I just keep... I keep replaying things in my head. Like, every time I've had to miss a family plan because I was too tired, or every time my husband and I have had a tense conversation recently. I just... I start feeling like I'm really letting everyone down. Like I'm failing as a wife, and as a mother, and even as a manager, even if no one is explicitly saying that to me. 

I try to tell myself it's just in my head, but it's hard to shake that feeling of just... not being good enough right now. Does that sound like a normal thing to go through when you're feeling this tired? I really hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than it is.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood, fatigue, and loss of interest in your hobbies?

Um, well... I hope I'm giving you the right timeline, I really want to make sure I'm giving you accurate information. I'd say this... this current slump has been going on for about a month now. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because right before this, I was actually doing so well. I was, um, unusually energized and just really driven, getting a ton done at work and at home. I felt like I was really on top of everything. And then it just sort of... swung into this persistently low feeling over the last four weeks or so. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm just complaining about one bad month, because I know people go through much worse and I should be able to just shake it off. Everyone has off months, right? Am I making sense with how I'm explaining this?
Before this current slump, have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?

Oh, um... yes, I have. I hope it's okay to admit that. I always try to push through those times and keep a smile on, so I don't burden anyone else, but... yes, there have been other times. 

The... the longest stretch I can clearly remember was a few years ago. It lasted for, gosh, about five months, I think? I just felt really low and tired, and just... very unlike myself most days. I still went to work and took care of the kids, of course—I'd never want to neglect my responsibilities! But it was like wading through mud the whole time. 

I'm sorry, I know five months sounds like a really long time to just let myself feel that way without fixing it. I really did try to snap out of it. Does it... does it make me sound terrible that it went on for that long? I promise I'm usually a much more positive person than this makes me sound.
Before that five-month period a few years ago, had you ever experienced a time when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two weeks at a time?

Um, before that... gosh, I really want to give you the right answer here, but I don't think so? I mean, I've had normal bad days, of course, like anyone else. But nothing that lasted for weeks on end like that time. 

I've always tried to be the kind of person who just bounces back, you know? I really try not to let things get me down for too long if I can help it. So, no, I don't recall any other long stretches like that before the five-month one. I hope that's helpful? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can.

Before this current period of feeling down, have you ever had a time when your mood was unusually high or you felt extremely energetic, maybe even more than usual, where you didn’t need much sleep or felt like you could take on the world?

Um, well... I guess I did mention earlier that right before this slump, I was feeling really good. I hope it didn't sound like I was bragging or anything. But yes, earlier this month, I had this... this unusually charged, upbeat mood. 

I felt just, I don't know, brilliant? Like I had all these great ideas and the energy to just go, go, go. It was actually really productive, which is a good thing, right? I got so much done. 

Though... I feel a little bad admitting this part, but I did get a little... snappy, I guess? If my husband questioned any of my plans or couldn't keep up, I'd get irritated really fast. I'm usually very patient with him, I promise! I just felt so driven, and it was frustrating when things slowed me down. I feel terrible that I was irritable with him, though. Does that make me sound awful? I really try to be a good partner.
